priceSnapshot.note: Down 0.40 percent on the 24h open of 78,869.3, and DOWN 587.7 points - 0.74 percent - against the 79,140.7 midday read six hours and forty-five minutes ago. Unlike midday, this is not a flat number hiding a round trip; it is a genuine leg lower. Price ran up to 79,366.1 shortly after the midday publication, failed there, and then broke down through the 20:00Z bar to 78,174.5 and through the 21:00Z bar to 77,854.1 - a new 24h low and 273.5 points BELOW midday's stated 78,127.6 invalidation. It was reclaimed inside the same hour, closing 78,567.7, which makes this the THIRD sweep-and-reclaim of a stated invalidation level today. The day's shape is now unambiguous: lower highs at 80,726.8, 79,571.4, 79,366.1 and 79,003.0, against lows at 78,127.6 and then 77,854.1.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from ADD back to REDUCE, and this time the reason is not a gate technicality but a genuine deterioration. Midday's own reduce gate did NOT fire by the letter: it required a settled 1H close below 78,536.1 with no reclaim on either of the next two bars, and while the 20:00Z bar closed 78,197.9 - satisfying the first clause - the very next bar closed 78,567.7 and reclaimed on the first of the two permitted bars. Midday's add gate at a settled close above 79,571.4 also never came close; the highest close since publication is 78,930.6. So neither gate fired, and yet the position changes anyway, because three things that were NOT in either gate have moved against the long side. First, price has lost the 1H EMA50 at 78,691.11 as well as the EMA20 at 78,984.07 - at midday it was above the EMA50 by 448 points and is now 138.1 points below it. Second, the 4H MACD histogram is not merely deteriorating, it is accelerating: minus 155.63, minus 170.25, minus 224.07, minus 287.45, minus 325.89. That is the worst reading of the entire leg and the rate of decay is increasing. Third, open interest has turned back UP by 1.07 percent to 2,287,101,452 USD while price fell 587.7 points over the same window, which is fresh positioning being added into weakness rather than the clean deleveraging midday measured. The honest counterweight is recorded in the divergences array and it is a real one, so this REDUCE is 10 percent of the core, not a liquidation.

overnightRisk: The gap to the next report is roughly six and a half hours and it opens with price 244.2 points - 0.39 hourly ATRs - above a live reduce gate, which is the tightest this desk has run into an overnight all week. Four specific things could resolve it badly. FIRST and most concrete, the 78,250 liquidation bucket is still actively taking fills: 289 of them, 99.7 percent long, with the most recent stamped 00:10:15Z, twenty-five minutes before this snapshot. Longs are being liquidated at a level 303 points below spot while this report is being written, which means the shelf immediately beneath is not a historical artifact but a live process. SECOND, the 21:07-21:08Z capitulation is the template for how fast this can move: 64 fills totalling 956,716 USD executed in the 77,750 bucket inside a 120-second window, and price covered 320.4 points from 78,174.5 to 77,854.1 in under an hour. A repeat of that in thin Asian-hours liquidity would take out the 77,854.1 invalidation without a human present to see it, which is precisely why the resting stop is flagged. THIRD, the ETF flow print is incomplete in a way that cuts both directions: Farside shows 25 Aug at plus 29.9m across the reporting issuers, but IBIT - which supplied 208.9m of yesterday's 337.6m and has been the single dominant line every day of the seven-day streak - is still showing a dash rather than a number. When IBIT posts overnight it will either extend a seven-day inflow streak decisively or break it, and the market will trade the difference at a moment when nobody is watching this book. FOURTH, funding at 0.0000950122900239 per eight hours sits BELOW the 0.0001 exchange floor with the perp premium at minus 0.00039098, so the perp trades under the spot index; that is a market with no long froth left to squeeze out, which is constructive, but it also means there is no crowded-short fuel for an upside squeeze either. The overnight is therefore asymmetric toward drift rather than either violent tail - but the tail that exists is the downside one, and it sits 699 points away.

liquidation.note: 3,250,128 USD across 175 fills and 100.0 percent of it LONG - not one short liquidation in the entire bucket. This is what a capitulation spike looks like in the raw feed, and it marks the exact 77,854.1 low. It is also the reason the recommended stop is placed at 77,650.0 rather than just under the low: a stop between 77,750 and 77,854 sits inside the sweep zone that has already proven it will be probed.

operations.note: Flat for the fourth consecutive session and this is the easiest of the four to justify. A long here needs its stop under 77,854.1, which is 699 points of risk for a first objective at 79,003.0 that is 450 points away - negative expectancy before the overnight gap is even considered. A short is worse on a different axis: it would be selling 699 points off a capitulation low into a market where 84.6 percent of all liquidations in fourteen hours have already hit the long side and where the 1H oscillator is diverging positively against that low. Neither side pays. The additional reason specific to this session is that the next mark is six and a half hours away with nobody watching, and a leveraged position with a resting stop in Asian-hours liquidity is exactly the setup that gets swept and then reverses.

Trim 10 percent of the spot core at 78,553.0 ahead of the overnight gap. This is not a reversal of midday's thesis, it is a size adjustment for the fact that the book is carrying its largest spot position of the round into the longest unmonitored window of the day, with price below both fast hourly moving averages and the 4H EMA20 rising into it. The trim is deliberately small - 10 percent, not 25 or 50 - because the bullish divergence on the 1H is genuine and because the 4H and daily structures are entirely intact.

The day's full sequence now reads: midnight bought 20 USDT at 80,726.8 and is down 2.69 percent, morning trimmed 10 percent at 79,161.2 and is right by 608.2 points, midday re-added 18 USDT at 79,140.7 and is down 0.74 percent, and endday trims 10 percent at 78,553.0. One correct call in four, and the correct one was a trim. That record is the honest reason this session leans defensive rather than buying the third sweep of the day: the desk has now bought two flushes today and been wrong on both, and a fourth session of adding into a market making lower highs and lower lows would be conviction overriding evidence.

divergences.note: The single most important counterweight to this session's bearish tilt, and it is measured rather than eyeballed. Price made its first low of the day at 78,127.6 on the 13:00Z bar with the 1H MACD histogram at minus 227.19. Eight hours later, on the 21:00Z bar, price made a LOWER low at 77,854.1 - 273.5 points beneath the first - but the histogram printed minus 172.82, a HIGHER low by 54.37. Lower low in price against a higher low in the oscillator is textbook bullish divergence, and it has extended since: the last three bars read minus 141.44, minus 136.97 and minus 135.54. This is why the endday stance is a 10 percent trim with a resting stop rather than a meaningful exit. It invalidates on a settled 1H close below 77,854.1, which would make the divergence a failed one.

calibration.note: Midday's reduce gate at a settled 1H close below 78,536.1 did NOT fire. The 20:00Z bar closed 78,197.9, satisfying the settled-close clause, but the 21:00Z bar closed 78,567.7 and reclaimed the line on the first of the two permitted bars, so the two-bar reclaim clause blocked it - the third time in one day that clause has filtered out a false trigger. Midday's add gate at a settled close above 79,571.4 was never approached; the highest close since publication is 78,930.6, short by 640.8 points. Midday's invalidation at 78,127.6 WAS breached, and more decisively than morning's was: price traded to 77,854.1, some 273.5 points below it, though it reclaimed inside the same hour and closed 440.1 points above. acting_helped is FALSE - midday's 18 USDT add at 79,140.7 is underwater by 0.74 percent, roughly 0.13 USDT. The instructive part is that midday's reasoning was sound on every input it named and still lost, because it weighted the spent-fuel argument correctly but did not price the possibility that a fresh shelf would be built lower. That is the lesson carried forward.
